exposure: duration of estrogen (E2) treatment prior to frozen-blastocyst transfer
cohort: The study included 1377 frozen-thawed blastocyst transfers using artificial endometrial preparation (AEP) with exogenous estrogen (E2), assigned to groups based on E2 administration duration.
finding: Live birth rate significantly decreased when estrogen (E2) exposure prior to frozen-thawed blastocyst transfer exceeded 28 days, and early pregnancy loss rates significantly increased when E2 exposure lasted more than 35 days.
